transcript:
Header: 2026-03-28 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Maya, Tom, Sara (Aventra)

Summary (auto): quick review of last week's baseline comparison; dug into p95 spikes, discussed tuning (batch size, KV cache ttl), agreed on dedicated perf runs.

[00:00] Alex: ok hi everyone, thanks for joining, we have about 45 minutes, quick agenda - benchmark review, tuning notes, and next steps. Maya, Tom, Sara you good?
[00:12] Maya: yeah all good, sorry running from a standup so may jump out if important stuff comes up.
[00:18] Tom: good.
[00:20] Ravi: hey team, i pulled together the perf slides and raw CSV, i'll share in chat after. note there are a couple of noisy samples in the baseline runs, probably network blips.
[00:30] Sara: perfect, thanks.

[02:00] Alex: ok first page - high level numbers for the 512 token generation scenario we tested. p50 for Redwood hosted was about 120ms, p95 around 420ms. baseline provider (BaseCloud) had p50 150ms, p95 620ms. throughput measured as tokens/sec at steady-state was ~18k tokens/sec for Redwood on the 4-GPU pod with batching, baseline was ~12k tokens/sec.
[02:38] Maya: curious, are those with or without KV caching?
[02:42] Ravi: those include prefix/kvcache for repeated contexts - we enabled caching for the 80% repeat traffic case. without cache p95 moves up ~30-40% for both.
[03:05] Tom: and the baseline p95 had the big spike at run 7, is that the network blip you mentioned?
[03:12] Ravi: yeah exactly, one of their runs had a 2.3s tail, we marked it as outlier in the summary but raw CSV has it.

[04:00] Maya: for us p95 is the big deal - peak latency affects our UI timeouts. can you break down what contributed to Redwood's p95?
[04:10] Ravi: sure - two main components: kernel scheduling / batching delays under burst, and occasional KV miss penalties. we saw that increasing the continuous-batching window from 10ms to 25ms reduced p95 by ~60ms at a slight cost to p50 (~10-15ms).
[04:35] Alex: right - tradeoff is latency tail vs amortizing GPU kernel overhead. for the customer facing UI you probably want p95 tuned; we can set adaptive batching.

[06:00] Sara: what about quantization? you mentioned INT8 runs gave throughput improvements?
[06:06] Ravi: yes - INT8 quantization on the model variant we used gave about 1.4x throughput improvement and p95 decreased by ~80ms in our runs. quality diff was minimal on your eval set; we flagged a couple of hallucination patterns but nothing material.
[06:40] Maya: how about retraceability - do we lose any logging or token-level cost breakdown when using quantized models?
[06:47] Alex: no, instrumentation is the same; cost accounting and token-level traces are preserved. quantization only affects model weights and execution path.

[08:00] Tom: can you explain the testing topology for the dedicated runs vs hosted? network geometry matters for us, we're in us-east-1 with a VPC peering setup to the baseline infra.
[08:12] Ravi: hosted runs were Redwood public endpoints in us-east-1, dedicated runs we spun a 4xA100 pool in the same region; baseline was a vendor-managed cluster in the same region but cross-az which introduced some network variance. we included in the notes the pod placement and NIC bandwidth.
[08:40] Tom: ok that explains some of the spikes. we'll want a dedicated run inside our VPC to measure egress and peering latency.

[10:00] Maya: any surprises on memory / GPU utilization? we need to know headroom for concurrency.
[10:06] Ravi: GPU mem was ~78% for the 4GPU pod on the float16 variant; INT8 brought mem down to ~62% allowing higher concurrency. CPU/socket for preproc stayed low. batch sizes we used were adaptive from 1 to 64 depending on inflight requests.

[12:00] Alex: quick note on autoscaling - Redwood Dedicated autoscaling reacts to queue length and token backlog. in the POC we tuned the policy to keep p95 under 500ms; you can tighten to 350ms if you want more nodes. tradeoffs with cost.
[12:25] Sara: yes we want a predictable SLA - can Redwood emit the same autoscale metrics to our monitoring (datadog)?
[12:33] Alex: yup, we stream per-route metrics and trace hooks; we'll share the Dashboard JSON.

[14:00] Tom: about security - we need confirmation on KMS usage for model keys and audit log retention. baseline vendor said 90 days retention only, do you support longer?
[14:12] Alex: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and configurable audit retention; hosted has defaults but we can enable 365-day retention on enterprise tier. we'll attach the security pack.
[14:30] Maya: also SSO requirements - SAML, RBAC mapping for the engineers.
[14:36] Lena (CSM): we have a SAML playbook and sample mapping; will include in the packet.

[16:00] Ravi: back to numbers - i want to call out p95 per run trend: over 10 sequential runs, Redwood p95 median was 410ms with IQR 35ms, baseline median 590ms with IQR 120ms. so baseline had larger variance.
[16:22] Maya: is that consistent across model sizes? we may be testing a larger 13B variant next week.
[16:29] Ravi: good question - for a 13B we expect absolute latencies ~1.6-1.8x of the 7B we tested; relative gains from INT8 hold but scheduling differences magnify tails. we recommend a run next week on your 13B workload.

[18:00] Tom: curious about fallback behavior - if dedicated capacity is saturated, does Redwood route to hosted auto-fallback?
[18:08] Alex: yes you can configure smart routing: primary dedicated, fallback to hosted or a cheaper model variant. we support automatic degrade policies and can keep token safety by restricting open-internet fallbacks.
[18:28] Sara: can we restrict to only Redwood-verified open models for fallback?
[18:31] Alex: yep, that's the default we recommend.

[20:00] Maya: quality monitoring - will Redwood alert if quality regression appears after quantization?
[20:07] Ravi: we have eval hooks and a quality monitor where you can pin prompt sets; we run reference evals and can trigger regression alerts. we'll add your prompt set if you share it.

[22:00] Tom: we skimmed the raw CSV earlier, but can you explain the columns? some column names seemed short.
[22:08] Ravi: sure - columns: run_id, timestamp, route, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, backend_p95_ms, net_lat_ms, gpu_util_pct, kv_hit (true/false). i admit some tooling clipped headers - raw CSV will have full headers.

[24:00] Maya: on cost - baseline provider quoted X for reserved capacity, how does Redwood compare for dedicated?
[24:06] Alex: we provided an estimate in the deck; in short, Redwood Dedicated with reserved commit is roughly 10-15% lower unit cost than that baseline due to batching and cache effectiveness, and the Optimize recommendations often reduce billable tokens. exact depends on your traffic profile.
[24:40] Sara: ok we'll need a formal quote once we finalize the target throughput.

[26:00] Ravi: action item: we'll run a dedicated INT8 test inside your VPC next week using the 13B workload and the same traffic pattern; we'll measure p50/p95 and tokens/sec and share logs.
[26:12] Tom: for the VPC test, we'll need the test subnet and peering details, Tom will send.

[28:00] Alex: quick demo note - small change we made in the runtime scheduling cut kernel launch overhead by merging small ops; that's in the notes under "kernel sel/opt". might be why you see better tail behavior.
[28:20] Maya: cool.

[30:00] Sara: any concerns about model drift or update rollouts?
[30:05] Ravi: rollouts are supported canary/A-B with automatic rollback on regression; we'll provide our rollout playbook.

[32:00] Maya: ok last part, next steps recap?
[32:05] Alex: recap: 1) Alex send raw CSV + annotated slides (by 4/1) 2) Ravi run dedicated inside Aventra VPC with INT8 13B workload (complete by 4/3) 3) Tom to send networking details + test dataset (by 3/30) 4) schedule follow-up week of 4/6 to review dedicated results and canary plan.
[32:40] Tom: confirmed i'll share peering details today.
[33:00] Maya: also please include Datadog dashboard JSON and security packet.
[33:06] Lena: noted, will include.

[35:00] Sara: ok thanks everyone this was useful.
[35:05] Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and upload artifacts to the shared drive.
[35:12] Maya: bye.

(Transcript ends - auto-generated; some speaker labels may be imperfect. Raw CSV and slides shared in chat link: https://redwood-internal/benchmarks/aventra-2026-03-28.csv)
